channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: What Does the Science Tell Us About Heated Tobacco Products? | #GFN26ScienceLab
item.description: The science on heated tobacco products sits in the space between cigarette harm and smoke-free innovation. These products still involve tobacco, but they do not burn it in the same way cigarettes do, making exposure data and real-world switching patterns essential. The key is not to overstate certainty or ignore risk, but to understand where they sit on the nicotine risk spectrum. Better regulation starts with that comparison. (Published on September 08, 2026bygfn.tv)

item.title: New Zealand decided to legalise pouches. Then nothing happened.
item.description: Legalising nicotine pouches was never supposed to cause a public health spectacle. New Zealand’s experience suggests that regulated access can simply give adult smokers another smoke-free option without the chaos often predicted by opponents. That matters because fear-based arguments frequently assume the worst before a product is even allowed to operate under rules. Sensible regulation can manage risk while still making room for alternatives that help move people away from cigarettes. (Published on September 08, 2026byconsideratepouchers.org)

item.title: Australia grapples with tobacco tax hike fallout
item.description: Australia’s tobacco tax fallout shows the danger of treating price as a standalone public health tool. Excessive excise can push smokers towards illegal cigarettes, strengthen criminal supply chains and weaken trust in regulation. The goal should be lower smoking, not a larger black market. Tax policy works best alongside realistic enforcement and legal access to lower-risk alternatives that make leaving combustion easier. (Published on September 08, 2026bysnusforumet.se)

item.title: How illegal tobacco is stealing profits from convenience store retailers
item.description: Illegal tobacco is not a side issue on UK high streets; it is becoming part of the retail landscape. Cheap illicit cigarettes undercut responsible shops, weaken age controls and move the market further away from oversight. That should worry anyone serious about public health. A credible tobacco strategy has to make legal routes away from smoking stronger than the criminal supply chains keeping combustible tobacco cheap and accessible. (Published on September 08, 2026byconveniencestore.co.uk)

item.title: The Global Regulatory Paradox of Cannabis Versus Nicotine
item.description: The contrast between cannabis liberalisation and nicotine restriction reveals a deep regulatory inconsistency. Governments increasingly defend adult autonomy for cannabis while criminalising non-combustible nicotine products that can move smokers away from cigarettes. That double standard is hard to justify on harm reduction grounds, especially when combustion drives so much of the risk in both markets. Policy should be based on exposure, evidence and real-world outcomes — not on which substance happens to be more politically acceptable. (Published on September 08, 2026bygithub.io)
